articles.title: 2028 quarterback Owen Herrick commits to Illinois
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh quarterback chose the Illini over Nebraska, Ole Miss and Syracuse.
articles.body:
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Owen Herrick has made his choice.

The Class of 2028 quarterback committed to Illinois on Wednesday. Herrick attends Pittsburgh Central Catholic and gives Bret Bielema and the Illini their first hard commitment in the 2028 class.

Herrick is listed at 6-foot-2 and 185 pounds and is rated as a three-star prospect by 247Sports. The website ranks him as the No. 29 quarterback nationally and the No. 12 prospect in Pennsylvania. He held ten offers before choosing Illinois, with Nebraska, Ole Miss and Syracuse among the programs in his recruitment.

With Sladen Shack already in the 2027 class, Herrick gives Bret Bielema and the Illini another quarterback piece to build around in the future.

For Herrick, the message after making his decision was pretty simple: "I'm home!! I-L-L."

articles.title: Nico Collins Injury Update, New Rumors on Texans WR Before Week 2 vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Heading into Week 2, the Houston Texans are dealing with an injury to one of their top offensive weapons.
articles.body:
Heading into Week 2, the Houston Texans are dealing with an injury to one of their top offensive weapons.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, Nico Collins was limited at practice on Wednesday because of a hamstring injury. Aaron Wilson of KPRC2 noted that Collins will have tests done to determine the severity of the injury.

Collins had a strong start to the season, recording seven receptions for 75 yards and a touchdown in a 36-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

The good news is Collins was still able to go through individual drills, so the injury seemingly hasn't impacted his mobility too much.

Collins is coming off his third consecutive season with 1,000-plus receiving yards, recording 1,117 yards and six touchdowns as Houston reached the playoffs for the third year in a row.

The Texans' receiver room already took a hit before the season when Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL in August, ending his year before it even started. Higgins was the team's third-leading receiver as a rookie.

It doesn't seem like Collins is looking at a lengthy injury like Higgins', but it's at least something to monitor heading into Week 2.

If Collins is unable to suit up this week, the Texans will look to Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson to make up for his absence. Boutte had just one reception for 21 yards in Week 1, while Hutchinson had three catches for 32 yards.

The Texans have their work cut out for them on Sunday as they face a Cincinnati Bengals offense that looked solid in a Week 1 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Being without Collins would make keeping up with the Bengals' offense even more difficult.

articles.title: Raiders dominance of Dolphins in the trenches a promising sign after last season’s line woes
articles.summary: Quarterback Kirk Cousins and running back Ashton Jeanty attracted much of the attention for the Las Vegas Raiders ' season-opening victory over Miami on Sund...
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. (AP) — Quarterback Kirk Cousins and running back Ashton Jeanty attracted much of the attention for the Las Vegas Raiders ' season-opening victory over Miami on Sunday.

Beyond that, Las Vegas also got the best of the Dolphins on the offensive and defensive lines.

It was that dominance that not only helped make the difference, but provided a promising sign for a team that entered the season with so many questions about both areas.

Not that those questions have completely gone away. The Dolphins are facing a rebuild, and starting with Sunday's trip to the Los Angeles Chargers , the Raiders are about to begin a six-game stretch against opponents that will help define their season.

But the fact both lines stood up so well is still something to build upon.

"I thought our guys were detailed," said coach Klint Kubiak, making the point he also was including the entire team. "They were prepared for the game, and they played hard. The effort was what we expected to be, and it's got to stay that way."

There were more questions about the offensive front than the defensive line. Las Vegas' offensive line was statistically the league's worst last season, allowing 64 sacks and averaging 77.5 yards rushing per game and 3.57 yards per carry.

Against Miami, the Raiders didn't allow a sack and the ground game produced 143 yards between Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr.

Improving the front was a priority for general manager John Spytek, who most notably signed center Tyler Linderbaum . The three-time Pro Bowler put together some highlight-reel blocks, including coming off one to quickly pivot to his right and keep Dolphins edge rusher Chop Robinson from getting to Cousins. What could've been a sack or batted pass instead became a touchdown toss to Jack Bech .

"Whenever you start with a win, you obviously can say there's a lot of good things that we did," Linderbaum said. "But also you've got to find things we need to improve on and get better at. It's a long season. The teams that get better each and every week are the teams that are going to be successful. There are a lot of things I think we could've done a lot better in the second half, and we've got to be able to finish games."

The fourth quarter, in particular, was a rough one for the offense. Las Vegas didn't score in that period and had just two first downs and 3 yards.

But the Raiders' defense seemed to only grow stronger as the game went on, pressuring Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis throughout and sacking him five times.

Largely because of the presence of Maxx Crosby , there weren't as many questions about the defensive line, but there were some. He's accustomed to facing double teams and chip blocks, but having another defender on the line who also can get into the backfield could force opposing offenses from devoting so much time into stopping Crosby.

Kwity Paye , who signed in the offseason, had two sacks and four quarterback hits. Crosby went from a quiet first three quarters to his usual menacing self with 1 1/2 sacks in the fourth.

"I know that going into the game, (Paye) doesn't maybe get as much hype," Kubiak said. "But all he's done this whole training camp has been available, practicing hard, being a great teammate."

Paye had 16 1/2 sacks combined in the 2023-24 seasons in Indianapolis , though he had just four last season.

"I think it's rewarding, kind of proving the front office right for wanting to come and get me," Paye said of his performance.

Crosby is accustomed to not coming off the field, but he played in 81.8% of defensive snaps against Miami. He underwent knee surgery in January, and Kubiak is being careful with not overloading his defensive superstar.

Such an approach would not have been embraced by Crosby in past seasons.

"From Klint to the coaching staff to the doctors, they want me to play for a long time at a very high level," Crosby said. "That's what I want as well. I'm in my eighth year. I could go out there and play 100% of the snaps. Is that the smartest thing to do? Probably not."

Backup quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the top pick in this year's draft , stood next to QBs coach Mike Sullivan on the sideline when the offense was on the field. Mendoza also wore his helmet so he could hear the play calls.

"I think it's important to hear it through the helmet because it simulates the real thing as opposed to the earpiece," Cousins said.

Tight end Brock Bowers (knee) and cornerback Darien Porter (foot) did not practice Wednesday. Kubiak said both remain day to day. Bowers didn't play in the opener and Porter was injured in that game.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ Shailene Woodley comments take an unexpected turn as podcasters struggle to make sense of his confession
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers has never been someone who shies away from controversy. But what he said on Cam Heyward's \"Not Just Football\" podcast last week genuinel.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has never been someone who shies away from controversy. But what he said on Cam Heyward's "Not Just Football" podcast last week genuinely threw people off. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback revisited his broken engagement with actress Shailene Woodley, and the details he shared stopped sports fans and entertainment followers dead in their tracks. Within hours, social media was flooded. Podcasters were scrambling. And the version of events that the public had accepted for years suddenly looked very different.What exactly did Aaron Rodgers say about Shailene Woodley on the podcast?Aaron Rodgers laid it out plainly. He said he proposed to Woodley in December 2020, she said yes, and then just days later, she told him something he clearly never forgot. "I proposed, and she says yes… But a couple of days after that, she tells me, 'You know, before we get married, I gotta go fu--ing this guy,'" Rodgers said on the show.He did not name the person. That detail alone sent the internet into a spiral.Beyond that admission, Rodgers pushed back on how the split has been framed publicly for years. The narrative, as most people understood it, was that Rodgers left Woodley emotionally destroyed. He rejected that entirely. He said Woodley had removed her engagement ring by March 2021, barely four months after he proposed, and later told him directly, "I don't want to be with you." In Rodgers' version of events, there was no dramatic exit on his part. The relationship had already quietly ended before the public knew anything was wrong.Woodley, for her part, did not get into specifics when approached about his comments at a pre-Emmys event in Los Angeles. She reportedly laughed and walked away. No statement, no rebuttal.Why are podcasters and fans still talking about the Rodgers-Woodley confession days later?Because the mystery of the unnamed man is impossible to ignore.Maria Ciuffo and Francesca Mariano of the Chicks in the Office podcast captured what most people were feeling. Ciuffo said it plainly: "I can't wrap my head around this and immediately your brain starts going, who? Who was she talking about?" Mariano pushed the question further, wondering aloud whether this was someone Woodley had history with or someone she had simply been thinking about."Here's the question, do we think it's somebody she's already slept with, and it's like this guy was fu-king amazing, or it's someone that's just been on her wish list?" Mariano said. "It is hilarious, though, if she just had one fucking guy in mind."Ciuffo took it one step further, joking that the only thing that could top Rodgers' confession would be Woodley identifying the person herself. "Imagine Shailene Woodley just got online and was like, 'listen, I wanted to fuck Miles Teller,'" Ciuffo joked.That response, funny as it was, pointed to something real. Rodgers handed the public a story with no ending. He gave the what but not the who. And in 2026, that kind of open-ended revelation does not stay quiet. It gets picked apart, debated, and turned into content for days.What makes this moment genuinely interesting is not just the confession itself. It is that Rodgers chose to say this now, four years after the breakup, right as a new NFL season begins. Whether that was calculated or just unfiltered honesty is a question only he can answer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Could Geno Smith help the Jets break decade-long trend to go 2-0? A human skeleton could help explain the turnaround
articles.summary: Against the Packers this week, the veteran QB will lean on a secret weapon he discovered in a middle-school art class.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. — Geno Smith remembers the skeleton.

Not the proverbial skeletons of past seasons buried, the New York Jets ' back-again quarterback remarkably void of negativity or defiance about his winding NFL journey, offensive coordinator Frank Reich says.

Instead, this skeleton far predates the Jets selecting Smith in the second round of the 2013 NFL Draft and far predates Smith losing his starting job in 2015 after a teammate's punch fractured his jaw.

The skeleton Smith remembers was life-sized, a replica of every bone in the human body. It stood at the front of his seventh-grade observational drawing class. Smith and his visual arts magnet school classmates were instructed to draw it — every rib and vertebrae, every muscle surrounding the bones, the precise curvature of the spine.

"We had to look at the skeleton and then remember it and draw it to scale," Smith told Yahoo Sports in June. "A lot of the art tests that I took were similar to that where you had to look at something and then memorize it and then paint, draw or whatever, sketch it from memory ….

"Every single bone, we had to draw it to scale. You had to remember. And it's not like you're just drawing a stick figure — a real skeleton is a big deal."

And Smith's photographic memory, his two middle school art teachers told Yahoo Sports, ensured he didn't omit details.

The Jets do not need Smith to draw skeletons as they work to bury their franchise's many. But sitting in a hallway of the Jets facility during mandatory minicamp in June, this decades-past art project came to mind when Smith was told about Reich's early impressions of his quarterback.

"I think the guy's got a photographic memory, I swear," Reich had told Yahoo Sports earlier that day.

Smith didn't argue the claim: "I'm pretty sure I do, yeah."

He's known that, he says, since middle school art class.

That photographic memory was one of several factors that helped the Jets to a 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans , Smith comfortably completing 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards and no turnovers in his first game despite playing in his third offensive system and for a third team in three years.

But Smith has also learned as recently as last year — when his Las Vegas Raiders beat the eventual AFC champion New England Patriots in their season opener, before finishing the year 3-14 — that a successful Week 1 win does not a successful year make.

As he looks to lead the Jets to their first 2-0 start in 11 years, Smith will use his deeply entrenched memories of past games against Jonathan Gannon's defenses to take on the Green Bay Packers and their first-year coordinator.

But he'll also find confidence in the pieces around him, as his skill position and offensive line support far exceeds what Smith played with last year in Las Vegas .

"I'm super competitive and I'm super motivated, but also I understand it's a team game," he said. "And I understand it's a process and it's not just me alone."

One key to Jets' win vs. Titans: nearly doubling their usage of play action

When the Raiders traded Smith to the Jets in March, Smith thought back to his conversations with former Seattle teammate and now Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker .

Together, he says, they'd admired Jets running back Breece Hall .

"Kenneth really has a lot of respect for Breece and I do as well," Smith said. "And I was like, 'Man, he's nice.'"

The Jets' running game, compared to what Smith witnessed with the Raiders, is nice, too.

Determining the root of Las Vegas' dead-last offense in scoring and yardage is a tall task. But wherever the rot started, one place it went was clear: No team rushed for fewer yards than the Raiders' 1,317. No team allowed more sacks than the Raiders' 64.

So as Smith got his latest fresh start, in his original NFL home, he looked to the Jets' 10th-ranked rushing attack in 2025 and smiled.

"It's going to be my best friend," Smith said.

Beating the Titans, who also won just three games last year, is no panacea. But the Titans' run defense ranked above average last year, and the Jets gashed Tennessee for 152 yards, seventh-most in the NFL's opening weekend.

That run game, led by Hall's 102 yards and a touchdown, opened up the play-action threat.

"Massive help to any quarterback," Reich said of the run game in June. "It just takes the pressure off. It slows the rush down. You're in favorable down and distance more often. You get better chunk plays because you've got play-action pass that is set up for the quarterback, and Geno's got the arm that can get the ball down the field.

"So on some of that play-action pass stuff where you're trying to get the ball down the field, that kind of feeds momentum. So I think it's going to be a good fit."

Through one week, Reich's predictions panned out.

After taking 3.7 sacks and facing 7.9 pressures per game last year, Smith was not sacked and was pressured just once against the Titans, per Pro Football Reference .

A year after New York ranked 29th using play action on 19.3% of snaps, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, Reich nearly doubled that to 37.5% against the Titans — third-most among teams in the opening week.

And those chunk plays? Smith completed a whopping four passes for 20+ yards.

He aired a 40-yard pass to a diving Adonai Mitchell in the red zone in the third quarter and set up rookie Omar Cooper Jr. on a wheel route on third-and-9 for a 30-yard gain. Garrett Wilson caught two explosive passes from Smith: for 31 yards down the right sideline early in the third quarter and then 22 yards hugging the left sideline over the head of a defender the next drive.

"I thought he did an outstanding job," head coach Aaron Glenn said. "Listen, there's some things obviously that we've got to clean up and get better at. But man, I think he was dang-near 80% throwing the ball. He put the ball where he needed to. Some of those anticipated throws that he made, I mean the one to [Mitchell], the deep corner route, the ball was out of his hand, [Mitchell] was still actually running his route, and that comes down to trust. That's all that is is trust.

"That's been a work in progress from OTAs to training camp, still going into the season, and you're starting to see that actually show up quite a bit."

Smith swapping ideas with Reich, teammates to win 'chess game'

Winning one game far from guarantees Smith's NFL and Jets future.

While the 35-year-old plans to play for a while, there's reason to believe the Jets don't plan to play with him for the long haul.

The Jets own three first-round draft picks in the quarterback-rich 2027 draft after trading away All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner and All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams last year.

A young core, including Cooper, and first-round rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who scored a touchdown Sunday, appear to position the club to support its next man under center better than its last handful.

Until then, the Jets expect Smith to upgrade their arm talent, veteran presence and command in the huddle. He craves a chance to rewrite his own career after the Seahawks shipped him to Las Vegas in favor of Sam Darnold and then Smith threw a league-high 17 interceptions with the Raiders. Amid the instability and on-field dysfunction, Smith says he learned last year more about his teammates' responsibilities.

"I was around a lot of young players last year, a lot of rookies, and so I found myself coaching and probably getting the jump on my next life," Smith said. "I was coaching a lot last year, and when you have to do that, it just amplifies. You think in a different way. You see the game differently."

He aims to apply those nuances about his running backs' steps as well as his receivers' splits and hip angles to support the Jets this year, Smith far from a passive observer in building this offense.

Dating back to the spring, Smith and Reich have exchanged late-night voicenotes and clips to share how each has beaten certain concepts in the past, and how that informs their beliefs on strategy for the 2026 Jets.

He's sent teammates play clips, too, that skeleton-tested photographic memory coming in handy for not only Smith but those around him.

"I'll send them some videos or try to put some stuff on their iPads and they do the same," Smith told reporters Wednesday. "I think that open line of communication is great. It just breeds for a better offense and a better connection with the wideouts, running backs and tight ends."

Smith will again call upon that memory this week as the Packers arrive at MetLife Stadium in their second week under Gannon.

Smith faced Gannon's defenses four times when Gannon was Arizona 's head coach and Smith was playing for Seattle. Smith won all four times — including a fourth-quarter comeback in the 2023 regular-season finale.

Dating back to the spring, Smith and Reich were exchanging messages about his 2023 fourth-quarter situational work, quarterback sending coordinator the answers he found to chess matches from his prior chapters.

"You got to almost be thinking ahead in those situations," Smith said. "And you're almost thinking about, like, you try to get inside the defensive coordinator's brain. 'In this situation, the percentages are that he's going to make this call or do this thing. Well, here's our answer for that.'

"I love that about football because it's a chess game."

A chess game that Smith can, and will remember as he tries to give Jets fans their first 2-0 start in over a decade.

"Just looking forward to another opportunity to compete with the guys and go out there and try and win a game," Smith said. "Each and every week, it's about having a 1-0 mindset."

articles.title: How Travis Kelce got robbed twice? First at home, then by a $35 million ponzi scheme
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce is used to getting hit on the field. Off it, apparently, he never saw the hits coming. On Tuesday, a federal court in St. Louis revealed .
articles.body: Travis Kelce is used to getting hit on the field. Off it, apparently, he never saw the hits coming. On Tuesday, a federal court in St. Louis revealed that the Kansas City Chiefs tight end was among the victims of Siddharth Jawahar, a 38-year-old Texas-based investment adviser sentenced to 11 years in prison for running a Ponzi scheme that pulled in more than $35 million from investors. Jawahar was also ordered to pay $31.35 million in restitution. For Kelce, this marks the second time in under two years that someone helped themselves to what was his.What was the $35 million Ponzi Scheme Travis Kelce got caught in?Jawahar ran Swiftarc Capital LLC, an investment firm registered in Texas. Starting in 2015, he funneled nearly all client money into a single overseas bet -- Philip Morris Pakistan (PMP). At one point, 99% of investor funds sat inside that one position. When PMP's value fell off a cliff, Jawahar did what fraudsters do: he lied. He told clients their money was growing. Then he used fresh investor cash to pay off the older ones. Court records put the total taken from investors at $35,607,984. Only around $10 million was ever actually invested.A 2021 Forbes article had already flagged that Kelce was an investor in a Swiftarc fund. But the extent of his losses was never disclosed in court. Prosecutors noted a policy of not discussing individual victims in detail. What is known is that between July 2016 and December 2023, Jawahar kept the scheme alive while living well off other people's money -- private jets, luxury apartments in Austin and New York City, private club memberships, Gucci runs, and high-end restaurant tabs. When authorities closed in, he allegedly tried to coach a victim into giving favorable statements to the FBI, lied about his immigration status, and attempted to have his iPhone wiped remotely.U.S. District Judge Zachary Bluestone called the losses "enormous" during sentencing and cited the fraud's length as a key factor in the prison term. One victim told the court that Jawahar had "weaponized" their trust. His attorney told ABC News: "Sid Jawahar is a very good man, who has made some very serious mistakes and is taking ownership of all of it." The FBI and Manhattan District Attorney's Office investigated the case jointly.How did Travis Kelce's home burglary in 2024 compare to this?Before this week's courtroom revelation, Kelce was already dealing with a more physical kind of theft. On October 7, 2024, while the Chiefs were hosting the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football, someone broke through the rear door of his $6 million Leawood, Kansas home. What initially looked like a $20,000 cash grab turned out to be worse -- later reports confirmed that burglars also took roughly $100,000 worth of jewelry and his first Super Bowl jersey.The timing was deliberate. Investigators later determined that a criminal network had been tracking professional athletes using game schedules, hitting homes while players were guaranteed to be away. Kelce's teammate Patrick Mahomes was robbed within 48 hours too. Seven men were eventually charged in connection with a broader spree that hit NFL and NBA players across multiple states.Two separate crimes. Two very different methods. One common thread -- Kelce's name kept showing up on the wrong side of the ledger.His exact financial loss from the Swiftarc scheme remains undisclosed. What is clear is that federal prosecutors thought the connection relevant enough to name him in open court during sentencing. For someone who built a brand around being untouchable on the field, the last two years have shown that wealth doesn't come with a security guarantee -- physical or financial.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Good Riddance!’ ‘Deserved Punishment’ — NFL Fans React as 2 Super Bowl Champions Are Removed From Hall of Fame Voting After ‘Unforgivable Mistake’
articles.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame has changed how its selection committee is going to look, and the timing has brought renewed scrutiny to one of the most debate...
articles.body:
The Pro Football Hall of Fame has changed how its selection committee is going to look, and the timing has brought renewed scrutiny to one of the most debated decisions in its recent history.

The committee is being reduced significantly after some uproar over Bill Belichick missing out on the Class of 2026, creating another round of discussion about how Hall of Fame voters should evaluate football's biggest figures.

Tony Dungy and Bill Polian Among Voters Removed

The Hall of Fame is moving from a 50-member selection committee to 25 voting members and three non-voting members. The restructuring also removes guaranteed seats for writers representing each NFL market and changes how candidate presentations are handled.

Yahoo Sports reported that Hall of Fame coach Tony Dungy and Hall of Fame executive Bill Polian are among those no longer serving as selectors. Longtime voters John McClain and Frank Cooney were also removed after 33 years on the committee, while Lisa Salters and several other selectors were among those affected.

The changes came after Belichick, a six-time Super Bowl-winning head coach, failed to receive enough votes for the 2026 class.

For his part, Hall of Fame President Jim Porter said the timing of the changes was coincidental (going on for the last two and a half years). Reports and fan reactions, however, have connected the committee overhaul to the controversy surrounding Belichick's omission.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

One fan described the situation as a major failure for the Hall, writing on X , "The Belichick incident was an unforgivable mistake. The Pro Football HOF had to clean house in order to save their reputation."

The reaction soon became more personal toward Dungy and Polian. Another fan wrote , "Two absolute clowns and jokes of men. Hatred deep in their hearts, glad the HOF committee did the right thing."

Not every reaction focused specifically on the former Colts figures. One fan instead referenced the Patriots ' controversial history, writing , "Clear the way for the cheaters to join! We will remember the Pats saga as a dark, dirty era of football!"

The discussion then returned to the voting decision itself. "Deserved punishment after not voting in Belichick," one fan wrote .

Another offered a much shorter response to the committee shake-up : "Good riddance!"

Fans also pointed to Dungy and Polian's own Hall of Fame credentials while arguing that their roles as selectors created a different standard.

One wrote , "Two guys, both deserving HOFers themselves, who let their personal feelings and jealousy stop them from doing the right thing and letting Bill Belichick take his rightful place in the Pro Football Hall of Fame can't vote anymore. Good. I see no problem here."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

The strongest reaction invoked Belichick's coaching record and criticized the reported handling of his candidacy .

"Hallelujah. I don't care what you think about Bill Belichick; what he did as a coach for the Patriots makes him a Hall of Fame coach by any conceivable measure. What Dungy conspired to do and did was akin to a criminal act. He and Polian should be outcasts in the game."

The Hall's restructuring now leaves a smaller voting group, while the debate surrounding Belichick's exclusion continues to shape discussion about the selection process.

articles.title: Javonte Williaims Fined By NFL, Apologizes to Teammates For Week 1 Penalty
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams shares that he apologized to his teammates after giving away a costly penalty in Week 1. The post Javonte Willia...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys lost to the New York Giants 28-20 on the very first Sunday Night Football of the 2026 NFL season in a game that showcased sloppy play from the entire team.

And one clear example of this was when running back Javonte Williams , who signed a three-year, $24 million extension this offseason, taunted the opposing defense in the end zone after going in for a score.

Although the damage was hugely significant; it merely caused kicker Brandon Aubrey to miss the extra point that had to be taken 15 yards further back; it was emblematic of a slapdash performance on the evening.

As noted by Cowboys reporter Clarence Hill Jr., Williams spoke out about his reckless decision on Sunday night, noting that he has already apologized to his teammates.

Javonte Williams Accepts Responsibility for Taunting

"Cowboys running back Javonte Williams said he was fined by the NFL for the taunting penalty against the Giants. He said he apologized to his teammates and said it was out of character for him. He said it won't happen again because he is through celebrating." Hill posted on X on Wednesday.

"You don't have to worry about it no more. I'm done. It was my fault. I'm better than that." Williams was subsequently quoted as saying.

Williams' fine – per NFL rules – will have come to $11,941, the amount levied against players for a first-time taunting offense. Second offenses carry a fine of $17,911.

Williams Looking to Move Past Difficult Opener

For a player who was given $16 million guaranteed this past offseason, and who has already made nearly $12 million in his pro football career to date, a little shy of $12,000 is merely a drop in the ocean. But it does represent a bigger point about discipline concerns about this Dallas team, both on penalties and broader mental mistakes.

Whilst the 26 year old is coming off a career season in 2025 that saw him put up 1,201 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns, his performance on Sunday beyond the taunting penalty still left much to be desired. Williams rushed 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown.

The former North Carolina product will be looking for a bounce-back game this weekend when the Cowboys take on another division rival, the Washington Commanders .

articles.title: Colin Kaepernick claims Robert Kraft allegedly used the same Macklemore tactics against him in 2017
articles.summary: In light of Robert Kraft getting Macklemore banned from several NFL stadiums, Colin Kaepernick has suggested that the New England Patriots owner did the same...
articles.body:
In light of Robert Kraft getting Macklemore banned from several NFL stadiums, Colin Kaepernick has suggested that the New England Patriots owner did the same to him.

Kaepernick's decision to kneel during the national anthem in 2016 proved to be the end of his career, as the former San Francisco 49ers quarterback never got an opportunity to return to the NFL following the incident.

Kaepernick was not offered a contract by any NFL team in free agency, following which he filed an official complaint alleging collusion by NFL owners.

Colin Kaepernick suggests Robert Kraft did the same thing to him as he did to Macklemore

Recently, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft has come under fire for allegedly orchestrating a ban against Macklemore following his comments during an Ed Sheeran concert.

Speaking on the Meidas Touch podcast, Colin Kaepernick claims that this is exactly what Kraft did to him when he entered free agency in 2017.

"The part that I hope people appreciate and take away in this moment is what Robert Kraft and what they're saying by denying Macklemore the opportunity to go out and perform with Ed Sheeran is they are willing to collude. They are openly colluding.

"When we filed the grievance, it was like, well, the owners wouldn't do that,. Everybody just wants to win within the NFL.

"And the realisation is, no. They want to protect their interests. They want to protect their power. They want to protect their money.

"And they also want people to know that if you take an action that they don't agree with, they will come for you."

Kaepernick, as mentioned previously, filed a grievance against the NFL owners for colluding against him to keep him out of the league.

Two years later, in February of 2019, the NFL reached a settlement with Kaepernick over the matter. However, there was still no change on the league's stance about bringing him back.

While Kaepernick kept himself in shape and available to return to the league, no opportunity materialised. Now 38 years old, Kaepernick is unlikely to make a return to the NFL.
